citation.source: Commonly cited culinary convention — a pinch of salt in basic flatbread dough

metadata.notes: This repo's first real recipe to exercise the whole baking epic (flour.json/dough.json/combine_dough.json/knead.json), 2026-08-17 — deliberately an UNLEAVENED flatbread (no yeast), the honest anchor dish: real roti/chapati/tortilla-de-harina-style breads are made exactly this way (flour + water + salt, kneaded, rested, then cooked in a hot pan), and skipping yeast entirely sidesteps the real, named multi-ingredient-COMBINE engine limit (dough.json's own multiIngredientLimitNote) that blocks a genuinely LEAVENED bread recipe from being built yet — this is not a workaround or a lesser proof, it's a real, complete, correct dish in its own right.
metadata.spawnIdNote: dough-1 is this recipe's first and only spawn event (combine_dough's own combinesInto) — recipe-runner.ts's spawnCounter is global across the whole recipe, starting at 0 and incrementing per spawn regardless of entity type, so the first spawn in a recipe with no earlier PEEL/SEPARATE/etc. byproducts is always '<entityId>-1'. Verified by actually running this recipe (npm run recipe -- simple_flatbread), not hand-derived and assumed correct.
metadata.friedNotBakedNote: Cooked via FRY (a hot pan), not BAKE (an oven), even though dough.json asserts both isFryable and isBakeable — matching real technique: roti/chapati/tortilla-de-harina are traditionally griddle/pan-cooked, not oven-baked; a real oven-baked flatbread (pita, naan) is a genuine, different real dish this recipe does not attempt. oil-1 is included specifically because FRY's own requiredIngredientCapabilities (isFryingMedium) is unconditional — even a real, nearly-dry pan-fried flatbread commonly gets a light oil brushing, so this isn't fighting FRY's existing semantics, just choosing the closest real technique that satisfies them.
metadata.restNote: The 600s (10 minute) bench rest after kneading, before cooking, is real, common technique — letting the gluten relax makes the dough easier to roll/shape without springing back, the same real mechanism rest.json's own genericityNote already names for tortilla-de-patatas' combine-to-fry rest, applied here to a structurally different dish for a structurally similar reason (gluten relaxation, not heat/moisture redistribution).
